# package fxcm

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxcm"
```

Package fxcm is a UAFX ConnectionManager: OPC 10000-81 version 1.00.04, §6.7 to §6.16, §13 and Annex F.

A ConnectionConfigurationSet comes in as the Annex F structure uafx.ConnectionConfigurationSetConf, from a file (DecodeFile, F.2) or built in Go. NewConfig validates it and turns it into an immutable Config, one per Version of the set (§6.8.2). An Edit is the transactional edit of §6.7.4: a working copy that CommitUpdates turns into the next Version.

State is the state machine of a set (§6.9), with the transitions an action may start and the event each one has. The ownership classes of the ConnectionEndpoints a ConnectionManager finds (Ownership) and the decisions over them (what a run may close, when a lost response proves an endpoint ours, when a set may be processed again by itself) are pure functions, as are the diagnostics of §10.19 and the ConnectionState of §10.20.

A Manager holds sets and processes them against the AutomationComponents (§6.7.3, §6.7.5): it dials their servers through a Dialer, resolves the identifiers of a set (§13.3), and calls EstablishConnections and CloseConnections (§6.2.4, §6.2.5). Process starts a Run per set and returns at once; Status, the Observer and the Counters report what the runs do. An endpoint whose ownership a run cannot prove is Unresolved and never closed until Settle decides it.

The design of the ConnectionManager, which the comments cite as "design §n", is docs/design/uafx-connection-manager.md (go-opcua pull request 44).

## Functions

### func Activity

```go
func Activity(action uafx.FxProcess) uafx.LastActivityMask
```

Activity returns the LastActivity bit of the action (§10.30), 0 for an unknown action.

### func ConnectionStateOf

```go
func ConnectionStateOf(monitored, established bool, ep1 uafx.ConnectionEndpointStatus, ep2 *uafx.ConnectionEndpointStatus) uafx.ConnectionState
```

ConnectionStateOf returns the ConnectionState of a Connection (§10.20): NotMonitored when the ConnectionManager does not monitor it; NotEstablished when it is not established (before establishment, after removal, or when an endpoint disappeared); otherwise from the Status of its endpoints. For a Connection with two endpoints (bidirectional, or unidirectional with heartbeat, Figure 58): Initial when either is Initial, else Error when either is Error, else the lower of Ready, PreOperational and Operational. For an autonomous publisher or subscriber, ep2 nil (Figure 59): the state of ep1. A Status outside §10.17 is Error: library interpretation, fail closed.

### func DecodeFile

```go
func DecodeFile(b []byte) ([]*uafx.ConnectionConfigurationSetConf, error)
```

DecodeFile decodes the content of a ConnectionConfigurationSet file (F.2 Table F.37): a UABinaryFileDataType (Part 5 §12.31) whose Body is an array of ConnectionConfigurationSetConfDataType. The input is untrusted. An empty Body array returns no sets and no error. Any defect is ErrConfig with ua.StatusBadTypeMismatch in the chain (Table F.40). The sets are decoded, not validated: NewConfig does that.

The Namespaces of the file name the namespaces of the structures in it; Part 5 §12.31 maps its first entry to NamespaceIndex 1, and F.2 asks for [http://opcfoundation.org/UA/](http://opcfoundation.org/UA/) and [http://opcfoundation.org/UA/FX/CM/](http://opcfoundation.org/UA/FX/CM/) in it. DecodeFile requires the CM namespace and reads the Body with the indexes of Part 5. A compatibility tolerance, not a reading of F.2: when the Body does not decode that way and the first entry is [http://opcfoundation.org/UA/](http://opcfoundation.org/UA/), DecodeFile tries the indexes of a NamespaceArray (the first entry is index 0), as a writer that copies a server's NamespaceArray produces. A file without the OPC UA namespace, which F.2 asks for, is read too: index 0 is the OPC UA namespace either way.

### func Diagnose

```go
func Diagnose(name *ua.QualifiedName, action uafx.FxProcess, state uafx.ConnectionState, ep1 Outcome, ep2 *Outcome) *uafx.ConnectionDiagnostics
```

Diagnose returns the ConnectionDiagnostics of a Connection after a processing of its set with action (§10.19): the bit of the action in LastActivity, the others cleared; the Error bit when an endpoint did not succeed; per endpoint NoError and Good when it succeeded, its FxError and StatusCode when it failed, ProcessingStopped or Rollback with Good. ep2 is nil for a Connection without Endpoint2, whose fields are NoError and Good. state is the ConnectionState (ConnectionStateOf).

### func EncodeFile

```go
func EncodeFile(sets []*uafx.ConnectionConfigurationSetConf) ([]byte, error)
```

EncodeFile returns the content of a ConnectionConfigurationSet file for sets (F.2), which DecodeFile reads. Its Namespaces are [http://opcfoundation.org/UA/](http://opcfoundation.org/UA/) and the Data, AC and CM namespaces of UAFX. A NodeId in a set has the index of the Namespaces of its ServerAddress (F.1.2.2), not of the file, and is written as it is. The sets are not validated. Content larger than MaxFileSize is ua.StatusBadEncodingLimitsExceeded: DecodeFile would refuse it.

### func RetryAllowed

```go
func RetryAllowed(failures []Failure, unresolved int) bool
```

RetryAllowed reports whether a set in Error may be processed again by the ConnectionManager itself (design §5.5, decision D5): only when its last run failed, every failure of it is Transient (ProcessingStopped and Rollback follow from another failure and do not count), and the run left no Unresolved endpoint. An Unresolved endpoint stops automatic retries until a Reconcile or Settle clears it.

### func Scan

```go
func Scan(rec *EndpointRecord, obs *Observed, appURI string, preconfigured bool) (Ownership, ScanVerdict)
```

Scan returns the verdict of step 0 for an endpoint configuration that wants a preconfigured endpoint (IsPreconfigured, Table 79) or not, given rec (nil without one) and obs, the endpoint the browse found under the Name (nil when there is none), and the class of obs (Foreign when obs is nil).

### func StatusOf

```go
func StatusOf(err error) ua.StatusCode
```

StatusOf returns the StatusCode in the chain of err: Good for nil, ua.StatusBad for an error without one.

### type EditSlot

```go
type EditSlot struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

EditSlot is the edit state of one editable set (§6.7.4): at most one Edit, owned by the holder of the Lock. The zero EditSlot is a set that is not in edit, with the Lock at the ConnectionManager (F.1.3). An EditSlot is not safe for concurrent use: the ConnectionManager serializes the calls on a set.

#### func (EditSlot) Commit

```go
func (s *EditSlot) Commit(owner LockOwner) (cfg *Config, ok bool, err error)
```

Commit is CommitUpdates (§6.7.4): the working copy becomes the next Version of the set (Version is incremented on every commit, §6.7.4 and §6.8.2) and the Lock goes back to the ConnectionManager. ok is false when the set is not in edit: the call is ignored for the set and cfg is nil. The caller must hold the Lock, else ua.StatusBadInvalidState (Table 82).

Library interpretation: an invalid working copy, or one whose BrowseName or Folder changed (the identity of the set, §6.7.2; renaming is a Replace, F.3.3.2), is a \*ConfigError and the set stays in edit with the Lock at the owner, who may correct or discard it.

The flow Variables the edit changed are reflected onto the PubSubConfigurations of the set (§6.13.1, §6.16.3) as reflectFlows describes; a conflict there is a \*ConfigError too.

#### func (EditSlot) Discard

```go
func (s *EditSlot) Discard(owner LockOwner) (ok bool, err error)
```

Discard is DiscardUpdates (§6.7.4): the updates are dropped and the Lock goes back to the ConnectionManager. ok is false when the set is not in edit: the call is ignored for the set. The caller must hold the Lock, else ua.StatusBadInvalidState (Table 82).

#### func (EditSlot) Editing

```go
func (s *EditSlot) Editing() *Edit
```

Editing returns the Edit in progress, nil when the set is not in edit (Edit FALSE).

#### func (EditSlot) LockLost

```go
func (s *EditSlot) LockLost() bool
```

LockLost ends the edit when its Lock goes for any reason, such as the end of the owner's session or an expired Lock: the set is treated as DiscardUpdates (§6.7.4). It reports whether an edit ended.

#### func (EditSlot) Start

```go
func (s *EditSlot) Start(cur *Config, owner LockOwner) (*Edit, error)
```

Start is StartEditing (§6.7.4): the set goes into edit with the Lock given to owner and a working copy of cur. When owner already holds the Lock, nothing changes and Start returns the Edit in progress. Another owner's edit is ua.StatusBadInvalidState (Table 82).

### type EventKind

```go
type EventKind int
```

EventKind is the kind of an Event.

```go
const (
	// EventTransition: a set took Transition.
	EventTransition EventKind = iota + 1
	// EventCall: an EstablishConnections or CloseConnections call
	// returned; Method names it, Status is its outcome, Err a failure to
	// get one.
	EventCall
	// EventEndpoint: an endpoint was recorded, reclassified or forgotten
	// (Record; Closed when it was closed).
	EventEndpoint
	// EventSettle: Settle decided Record with Verdict.
	EventSettle
	// EventRetry: the set is processed again after Delay (RetryPolicy).
	EventRetry
	// EventMonitor: the monitor read a new Status of Record, or found it
	// gone (Err).
	EventMonitor
	// EventSetAdded: a set was added with Version 1 (Add, or ElementAdd of
	// Update).
	EventSetAdded
	// EventSetReplaced: a set was replaced by a new one of Version 1
	// (Replace, or ElementReplace of Update).
	EventSetReplaced
	// EventSetRemoved: a set was removed (Remove, or ElementRemove of
	// Update).
	EventSetRemoved
	// EventEditStarted: a set went into edit (StartEditing, §6.7.4).
	EventEditStarted
	// EventCommitted: the edit of a set was committed as Version
	// (CommitUpdates, §6.7.4).
	EventCommitted
	// EventEditEnded: the edit of a set ended without a commit
	// (DiscardUpdates, or its Lock went, §6.7.4).
	EventEditEnded
	// EventVerified: the verification of the records a Manager with a
	// Store loaded (design §6.4) decided Record (its new Class; Closed
	// when the record was dropped: its endpoint is absent or Foreign,
	// nothing was closed), or an attempt on the server at Address failed
	// (Err; Record nil).
	EventVerified
)
```

#### func (Manager) Close

```go
func (m *Manager) Close() error
```

Close stops the runs, retries and the monitor and closes the sessions. A run in progress, also the closes of a Replace or Remove, stops waiting for its calls (design §5.4: their outcome stays unknown) and ends in Error; Close returns after them. Later calls are ua.StatusBadShutdown.

#### func (Manager) CommitEdit

```go
func (m *Manager) CommitEdit(key SetKey, owner LockOwner) (*Config, bool, error)
```

CommitEdit is CommitUpdates (§6.7.4): the working copy becomes the next Version of the set. See EditSlot.Commit. A change of the Name of an endpoint that is established (has a record) is refused with ua.StatusBadInvalidState and the set stays in edit (§6.12: the CM rejects it while the Connection is established).

#### func (Manager) Process

```go
func (m *Manager) Process(action uafx.FxProcess, keys ...SetKey) []Started
```

Process starts the processing of the sets with action (§6.7.5) and returns at once, one Started per key in the order of keys: Err is ua.StatusBadNodeIDUnknown for a key without a set, ua.StatusBadNotSupported for an action that is not one of FxProcessEnum, ua.StatusBadInvalidState for a set in Processing (Table 86); Run is set when the run started. A set in edit is processed with its last committed Config (decision D7).

#### func (Manager) Reconcile

```go
func (m *Manager) Reconcile(key SetKey) Started
```

Reconcile starts a run that closes the known-owned endpoints of a set that its committed configuration does not need (survivors of an earlier Version or of a failed run, closes still pending) and checks its Unresolved endpoints again: one that disappeared is forgotten. It is a run without an Action of FxProcessEnum (ActionReconcile): transition 1 or 4 by vendor-specific means (§6.9.2).

#### func (Manager) Remove

```go
func (m *Manager) Remove(ctx context.Context, key SetKey) error
```

Remove removes a set (F.3.3.2 ElementRemove): CloseConnections with Remove TRUE for its known-owned endpoints, then the set goes. A set being processed or edited is ua.StatusBadInvalidState; no set of the key ua.StatusBadNoMatch. When a close fails, the set stays, in Error.

#### func (Manager) Replace

```go
func (m *Manager) Replace(ctx context.Context, conf *uafx.ConnectionConfigurationSetConf) (*Config, error)
```

Replace replaces a set (F.3.3.2 ElementReplace): conf is validated first, then the Connections of the old set are removed (CloseConnections with Remove TRUE for its known-owned endpoints), then conf becomes Version 1 of the set, in Ready, not processed. A set being processed or edited is ua.StatusBadInvalidState; no set of the key ua.StatusBadNoMatch. When a close fails, the old set stays, in Error, and the error has the StatusCode of the close (design §5.8).

#### func (Manager) Settle

```go
func (m *Manager) Settle(key SetKey, ep EndpointRef, verdict Verdict) error
```

Settle decides an Unresolved endpoint of a set (design §5.4). It is an administrative decision: the Manager never makes it itself. The Observer receives it. An endpoint that is not Unresolved is ua.StatusBadInvalidState; no such endpoint ua.StatusBadNoMatch.

#### func (Manager) StartEdit

```go
func (m *Manager) StartEdit(key SetKey, owner LockOwner) (*Edit, error)
```

StartEdit is StartEditing (§6.7.4) of a set for owner: the set goes into edit with a working copy of its committed Config. See EditSlot.Start.

```go
func (m *Manager) Update(ctx context.Context, ops []Operation, requireComplete bool) (applied bool, results []error)
```

Update applies a batch of operations as CloseAndUpdate does (F.3.3, design §5.8). First the whole batch is checked: one operation bit (FC-6, ua.StatusBadInvalidArgument; none ua.StatusBadNothingToDo), the names (ua.StatusBadBrowseNameDuplicated for an Add, ua.StatusBadNoMatch for a Remove or Replace), the state (ua.StatusBadInvalidState while processed or edited), and every new set. results has one error per operation, nil for success; applied is ChangesApplied of Table F.39.

Without requireComplete the failed operations are dropped and the others applied in order; a remove or replace whose close fails fails (the old set stays, in Error). applied is true when one or more operations were applied, false when none was.

With requireComplete nothing changes unless every operation is applied: applied is true when all were, false when none was (Table F.39). See updateComplete.

### type Options

```go
type Options struct {
	// Dialer opens the sessions to the servers of the AutomationComponents
	// (§9.2, §13.2). Required; ClientDialer is the default implementation.
	Dialer Dialer
	// ApplicationURI is the ApplicationUri of this ConnectionManager, the

	// Required.
	ApplicationURI string
	// ExclusiveApplicationURI asserts that no other ConnectionManager uses

	// proves an endpoint ours after a lost response (design §5.4). Without
	// it such an endpoint stays Unresolved.
	ExclusiveApplicationURI bool
	// CallTimeout bounds each EstablishConnections and CloseConnections call
	// (decision D6). 0: DefaultCallTimeout.
	CallTimeout time.Duration
	// RollbackTimeout bounds the rollback of a run. 0:
	// DefaultRollbackTimeout.
	RollbackTimeout time.Duration
	// Parallelism bounds the AutomationComponents called at the same time
	// by one run (§6.7.3.2 recommends parallel calls). 0:
	// DefaultParallelism.
	Parallelism int
	// MaxConnectionConfigurationSets limits the sets (§6.7.6). 0:
	// DefaultMaxConnectionConfigurationSets.
	MaxConnectionConfigurationSets int
	// Retry processes a set in Error again by itself (§6.9.1, transition 4
	// by vendor-specific means), only as RetryAllowed says. Nil: never
	// (decision D5).
	Retry *RetryPolicy
	// Monitor watches the ConnectionEndpoints of the established
	// Connections (§4.7.2, §10.20). Nil: ConnectionState is
	// ConnectionNotMonitored.
	Monitor *MonitorOptions
	// Observer receives what the Manager does. It must not block.
	Observer Observer
	// Logger logs at Debug what the Observer receives, and failures. Nil:
	// slog.Default().
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Store makes the Manager keep its sets, the records of its
	// endpoints, the journal of its runs and the intents of its calls
	// (design docs/design/uafx-persistent-connections.md §6): a set
	// change is durable before it is visible, and New loads them, every
	// endpoint record Unverified. A store that cannot be loaded, belongs
	// to another ApplicationURI or has a newer schema fails New. Nil:
	// memory only.
	Store fxstore.Store
	// StoreTimeout bounds each store operation. 0: 10 s.
	StoreTimeout time.Duration
	// Verify configures the verification of the records loaded from the
	// Store (design §6.4, §6.5): in the background after New, and as the
	// first step of every run of a set.
	Verify VerifyOptions
}
```

### type OwedWork

```go
type OwedWork struct {
	// Kind says what is owed.
	Kind OwedKind
	// Run is the run that owes it.
	Run RunID
	// Action is the action of that run.
	Action uafx.FxProcess
	// Address is the server of an unended call; empty otherwise.
	Address string
	// Names are the endpoint Names of an unended establish.
	Names []string
	// Changes are the operations of a set change (OwedSetChange): every
	// operation of the Replace, Remove or complete Update, which are made
	// together after the closes.
	Changes []PlannedChange
}
```

OwedWork is work the journal of a Manager shows, which it exposes and does not execute by itself (design §6.3): the first step of the next Process or Reconcile of the set does it (recover), and a Reconcile completes an owed set change. Until then it is reported and fences the operations that could bypass it.

### type Ownership

```go
type Ownership int
```

Ownership is the class of a ConnectionEndpoint a ConnectionManager finds under the Name of an endpoint configuration of a set. Library interpretation (design §5.3): only a KnownOwned or TakenPreconfigured endpoint may be closed; §6.12 makes the Name unique within a FunctionalEntity, which identifies an endpoint, not who made it.

```go
const (
	// Foreign: not made or taken by this ConnectionManager. Never touched.
	Foreign Ownership = iota
	// KnownOwned: this ConnectionManager created it, by the result of its
	// call or by the proof of ResolveLostResponse.
	KnownOwned
	// TakenPreconfigured: a preconfigured endpoint the set names as
	// preconfigured and a call of this ConnectionManager took. Closing it
	// with Remove TRUE releases it; the AC keeps it (§6.2.5.2).
	TakenPreconfigured
	// Unresolved: this ConnectionManager may have made it, without proof.
	// Reported, never closed, until a Reconcile or Settle decides it.
	Unresolved
	// Unverified: a record a Manager with a Store loaded at its start, not
	// verified against its AutomationComponent since (design
	// docs/design/uafx-persistent-connections.md §6.4, decision C3-D9).
	// Treated like Unresolved: reported, never closed, adopted or changed;
	// an establish fails the Connection whose Name it holds. Settle
	// decides it as it decides an Unresolved one.
	Unverified
)
```

The ownership classes.

#### func Classify

```go
func Classify(rec *EndpointRecord, obs *Observed, appURI string) Ownership
```

Classify returns the class of obs, found under the Name of an endpoint configuration of a set, given rec, the record of this ConnectionManager for that endpoint configuration (nil when it has none), and appURI, the ApplicationUri of this ConnectionManager.

  - With a record of the same NodeId, the class of the record, unless the endpoint no longer matches it: a KnownOwned endpoint whose ConnectionManagerApplicationUri is another is Unresolved, and so is a TakenPreconfigured one that is no longer preconfigured, is in use by another ConnectionManager (InUse), or has another ConnectionManagerApplicationUri: another ConnectionManager may have taken it since, and §6.2.5.2 keeping preconfigured objects does not make closing its Connection safe. Unresolved is reported and never closed, so that a takeover is seen, not undone.
  - Without a matching record, an endpoint with this ConnectionManager's ApplicationUri is Unresolved (§6.6.2 names an application, not a call); anything else is Foreign.

#### func ResolveLostResponse

```go
func ResolveLostResponse(lr LostResponse, appURI string, exclusive bool) (class Ownership, absent bool)
```

ResolveLostResponse decides an endpoint after a lost response (design §5.4). absent is true when nothing was created or taken. Otherwise class is KnownOwned only when all hold: the Name was absent at step 0, the browse finds exactly one endpoint, its ConnectionManagerApplicationUri is exposed and is appURI, the (AC, FunctionalEntity) was serialized for the run, and exclusive is true: the deployment asserts that no other ConnectionManager uses appURI (§6.6.2 identifies an application, which a redundant pair or a copied configuration may share). A preconfigured endpoint is TakenPreconfigured when exactly one is found, its RelatedEndpoint is the one the call set, and nothing says another ConnectionManager uses it (InUse, another ConnectionManagerApplicationUri). Everything else is Unresolved: fail closed.

#### func (Ownership) MayClose

```go
func (o Ownership) MayClose() bool
```

MayClose reports whether a ConnectionManager may close an endpoint of the class o (CloseConnections, §6.2.5): KnownOwned and TakenPreconfigured.

```go
func (o Ownership) String() string
```

### type Recovery

```go
type Recovery struct {
	// Pending is the number of records not yet verified.
	Pending int
	// Unverified are the endpoints whose records were loaded and not
	// verified: reported, never closed, adopted or changed. An unended
	// establish intent without an endpoint record holds its Names with
	// one (NodeID nil).
	Unverified []EndpointRecord
	// Owed is the work the journal shows. The first step of the next
	// Process or Reconcile of the set does it (a set change: a Reconcile
	// only); until then the set is not replaced, removed or updated
	// (Bad_InvalidState).
	Owed []OwedWork
	// Fenced is the work other sets owe that this set takes part in (an
	// operation of their set change), or that holds a server of this set
	// whose independence is not proven yet (fencedOf). While it is owed,
	// the remote operations of the set and its CommitEdit are refused
	// (Bad_InvalidState; library interpretation).
	Fenced []OwedWork
	// Unreachable are the servers (by Address) of Unverified records whose
	// last verification attempt failed, with its error; they are tried
	// again with a bounded backoff (VerifyOptions).
	Unreachable map[string]string
	// Blocked, when not empty, is why the remote operations of the set
	// are refused: a record of it in the store is not valid.
	Blocked string
	// Done: nothing is pending, owed or blocked.
	Done bool
}
```

Recovery is what a set owes and how far its records are verified (design §6.4).

### type VerifyOptions

